title: Below the Surface: Summarizing Event Sequences with Generalized Sequential Patterns

problem.claim: The paper studies succinctly summarizing a database of event sequences using generalized sequential patterns.

gap.claim: Usual sequential-pattern approaches are limited to observed surface-level events and do not additionally model generalized events that can match sets of events.

contributions.claim: The paper formulates summarization using the Minimum Description Length principle, seeking patterns and generalizations that compress the data without loss.
The paper proposes the heuristic Flock algorithm to efficiently find high-quality models for the resulting optimization problem.
Flock models dependencies among generalized events within patterns.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world data produce compact and interpretable models that accurately recover ground truth, including rare generalized patterns.
The authors report that Flock provides clearer insight into the data-generating process than state-of-the-art algorithms limited to surface-level patterns.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies succinct summarization of event-sequence databases.
It extends surface-level sequential patterns with generalized events that can match sets of events.
It uses Minimum Description Length to select patterns and generalizations that compress the data without loss.
Because exact optimization is difficult, the paper proposes Flock and reports compact, interpretable, and informative models in experiments.

source_observation.claim: The approach selects patterns and generalizations by optimizing lossless data compression under Minimum Description Length.

interpretation.claim: A compression-based objective can help control spurious and redundant patterns while preserving the represented data.

application.claim: Use an explicit description-length or comparable parsimony objective when designing compact sequence summaries.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this objective is suitable for settings where lossless compression or compactness is not the primary goal.

source_observation.claim: The reported models include generalized patterns and dependencies among generalized events, with clearer insight than surface-only algorithms.

interpretation.claim: Modeling abstractions above observed events may reveal structure in the data-generating process that surface-level patterns miss.

application.claim: When observed event vocabularies are fragmented or overly specific, consider patterns that match meaningful event sets and their dependencies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how generalized event sets should be defined or when they improve results outside the reported datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the optimization details or heuristic procedure used by Flock.
The abstract does not provide dataset names, quantitative results, baselines, or experimental settings.
